summary: S. 3897, the Officer John Barnes and Chief Michael Ansbro Public Safety Officers' Benefit Program Expansion Act of 2026, revises administrative procedures for the Public Safety Officers' Benefits (PSOB) program. It establishes processing timelines, requires interim benefit payments if deadlines are missed, mandates the use of subpoenas to obtain overdue agency records, requires ongoing outreach to public safety officers and underserved agencies, mandates the implementation of specific GAO recommendations, and requires annual audits of claims pending for more than one year.

affected_groups.effect: Receive clearer notification timelines for missing information, potential interim benefit payments if decisions are delayed beyond 270 days, broader ongoing program outreach, and potentially faster claim approvals if certified by the 911 Victim Compensation Fund or World Trade Center Health Program.
affected_groups.group: Public safety officers, disabled officers, and their survivors

affected_groups.effect: Subject to mandatory BJA subpoenas if they fail to provide requested information or documentation needed for claim adjudication within 30 days.

Must adhere to statutory deadlines for notices and determinations, issue interim benefits under certain conditions, conduct regular outreach, implement GAO recommendations, and report delay data to congressional committees.

key_provisions: Requires the Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA) to notify claimants of missing information within 90 calendar days of receiving a claim.
Requires the BJA to make a final eligibility determination within 270 calendar days after receiving all required information, or issue interim benefit payments if that deadline is missed.
Mandates that the BJA issue a subpoena to any public agency that fails to provide necessary information or documentation within 30 days of a request.
Requires the BJA to conduct ongoing outreach to public safety officers, disabled officers, and underserved public agencies, and report on reasons for any processing delays.

Requires the BJA to approve claims associated with the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund or the World Trade Center Health Program if specific certifications are provided, absent clear and convincing evidence to the contrary.
Requires the Attorney General to ensure the BJA implements specific 2024 GAO recommendations within 180 days.
Requires the Comptroller General (GAO) to conduct an annual audit of pending claims that have been unresolved for more than one year.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 3897, the Officer John Barnes and Chief Michael Ansbro Public Safety Officers' Benefit Program Expansion Act of 2026, revises administrative procedures for the Public Safety Officers' Benefits (PSOB) program. It establishes processing timelines, requires interim benefit payments if deadlines are missed, mandates the use of subpoenas to obtain overdue agency records, requires ongoing outreach to public safety officers and underserved agencies, mandates the implementation of specific GAO recommendations, and requires annual audits of claims pending for more than one year.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes the administrative timelines, oversight, and enforcement mechanisms for federal death, disability, and education benefits for public safety officers. It establishes legally binding response timeframes for federal agencies and creates mandatory investigative tools to speed up claims processing.
